title: Console surface prioritization: dashboards, sampled tracing, and cost rollups MVP
creator: Aisha Verma
description: Summary: This ticket captures a trimmed, implementation-focused scope for the Redwood Console observability surface that balances value for product teams with delivery speed. We are cutting higher-effort features (per-request token-level cost, full distributed trace integration, and historical per-route retention beyond 90 days) in favor of an MVP that provides: 1) compact dashboards for model & route level latency/throughput; 2) cost rollups by model and route (aggregate, adjustable by date); and 3) sampled traces that link to runtime logs. Purpose: unblock engineering work to meet Q2 go/no-go while preserving the core product promise: predictable unit economics and break-fix diagnostics for LLM inference.
out_of_scope:
- Per-token trace-level cost breakdown (deferred)
- Full open-telemetry ingestion + trace drilling (deferred)
- 1:1 mapping of function calls to structured output in console (deferred)
mvp_decisions: 1) Aggregate cost view by model and route is sufficient for initial cost investigations; per-token breakdown is a follow-up. 2) Implement sampled tracing (1% sampling by default) surfaced in Console with a link to detailed runtime logs in the infra dashboard. 3) Dashboard retention: 90 days for metrics and 30 days for sampled trace detail. 4) Feature gated behind console.observability.mvp flag for canary rollouts.
prioritized_feature_list: MUST: Dashboard - model & route cards with p50/p95 latency, throughput, error rate; Cost rollups - daily & 7-day aggregated cost by model/route; Sampled traces - show top-level span timeline + request id link. SHOULD: Time-range selector (last 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d); basic anomaly flags (spike detection). MAY: Per-environment filters (prod/staging). WON'T: Per-token cost, full trace explorer in MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboards: For any selected model, Console shows p50 and p95 latency and request throughput for the selected time window (24h/7d/30d/90d). Values update within 15s of backend response.
Cost rollups: Console displays aggregated cost by model and route for the selected date range. Cost numbers reconcile to billing within 3% for a 7-day sample dataset.

Tracing: Selecting a sampled trace opens a compact viewer with span timeline, top-level metadata (model, route, duration, error flag) and a single-click link that navigates to runtime logs filtered by request id.
Flags & rollout: Feature is guarded by console.observability.mvp flag and can be enabled per-org. Canary rollout to 5% of orgs with monitoring for errors/latency regressions over first 72 hours.
Performance: Dashboard API responses for aggregated views complete under 800ms p95 for cached queries and under 2s p95 for cold queries in staging load tests.
Security & compliance: No PII is shown in Console views. Logging link requires current org RBAC permissions; security review sign-off must be attached before wide rollout.
Instrumentation: All queries emit telemetry events with route/model tags and sampling indicator for trace samples (telemetry events available in observability pipeline).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary, 2 weeks): enable flag for internal orgs + 5% external customers; monitor errors, API latency, and cost reconciliation. Phase 2 (Wider rollout, 3 weeks): increase to 50% with support docs. Phase 3 (GA): enable by default for new orgs, migration docs for existing orgs.
design_notes: Figma frames: compact cards that emphasize latency and cost per model. Use chevron drill to open trace viewer. Design approved for MVP; follow-up UI improvements deferred. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/CONSOLE-OBS-MVP (placeholder)
engineering_notes: Backend: aggregator service must support time-windowed rollups and cost reconciliation endpoint. Add sampling hook into runtime to emit trace samples with request id. Frontend: lightweight cards + compact trace modal. See infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2857 (placeholder).
security_notes: Audit required for the log-link mechanism to ensure no sensitive payloads are exposed via Console URLs. KMS keys used for log access are org-scoped. Security reviewer: Elena Kowalski.
open_questions: Q1: What should the default sampling rate be in production? (engineering suggests 1%, support suggests 0.5% for high-volume orgs).
Q2: Do we need rate limits on the cost aggregation endpoint to protect the runtime from query storms?
Q3: How granular should role-based visibility be for cost numbers (team-level vs org-level)?
